notes: 1907 four-storey flats at the north corner of Allen Street. Brown smooth stucco, two cant bays near each end from storey 2 to the roof with flat paired windows under them on storey 1, a centre column of single hooded windows, dark brown trim. Ground: a central glazed entry under a brown awning, a wide window left, two small barred windows right. Allen return (edge 0) gets upper windows. Wall read pale pinkish grey against a clearly brown street; tint darkened, flank no longer inherits the entry awning. Deeper chocolate wall, espresso trim on frames, hoods, bay plates and cornice; brown sloped canvas awning over the centre door instead of the steel louvre; heavier cornice. Ground order is real viewer left to right (picture window, door, barred pair); awning moved to the neutral canvas kit (tinted awning-canvas read red). Wall pushed to a dark chocolate tint; near-black espresso on frames, sills, hoods, bay plates, cornice and shop frames; both cant bays now start at storey 1 and run to the roof; dark brown canvas awning with a valance over the centre entry, no pale stepped canopy; large dark-framed picture window and barred pair; dark bracketed cornice in the trim colour. Wall tint warmer and darker (less blue) so it stops reading mauve.
